verdict.rationale: Snowflake's docs index lists "connectors for ingesting and exporting data" alongside Snowpipe and COPY INTO, and dbt Projects on Snowflake gives first-party, documented support for one ELT/transformation tool. There is no evidence of which SaaS apps or databases are covered, of a partner connector ecosystem, or of setup guides for specific connectors. Snowpipe file loading and the JDBC/ODBC drivers are ingestion primitives, not source connectors, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documented first-party connectors for named SaaS apps and databases, a partner/ETL connector ecosystem (e.g. Fivetran-style integrations), per-connector setup documentation, independent corroboration of connector coverage.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, first-party and partner connectors cover my sources — SaaS apps, databases, and ETL/ELT tools — with documented setup

citations.quote: Stages, COPY INTO, Snowpipe, file formats, and connectors for ingesting and exporting data.
dbt Projects on Snowflake brings the full dbt lifecycle into Snowflake: develop, deploy, orchestrate, and observe your transformations in the same place your data already lives.
No infrastructure to manage: Snowflake provides managed dbt Core and dbt Fusion runtimes.
